newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Samsung still interested in Fokker - media.
newsitem.headline: Samsung still interested in Fokker - media.

text.p: South Korea's Samsung Aerospace is still interested in taking over bankrupt Dutch planemaker Fokker, according to Korean media on Monday, Dutch ANP agency reported.

Korean media said Samsung would re-start talks about a Fokker takeover in the New Year and cited Samsung as saying that, if the conditions were right, it remained interested in the Dutch firm which was declared bankrupt last March after Daimler-Benz withdrew financial support.
The South Korean government was also understood to have signalled financial aid for a Fokker takeover.
Fokker administrators, who have run the company for most of the year, broke off talks with Samsung in November after a series of deadlines expired with no firm word from the Koreans.
The final straw came when Northern Ireland-based Shorts, part of Canada's Bombardier said it would no longer supply wings for Fokker's regional jets.
Samsung was reported to have been mystified by the breakdown in negotiations.
Korean media said Samsung continued to seek partners in a Fokker takeover, with Daewoo said to be positive and Hyundai and Korean Air also mentioned.
Samsung sees a re-launched Fokker as a potential shortcut to the global aerospace industry, but has been reluctant to assume all the risks and wants substantial investment by the Dutch.

The Hague has indicated it might provide fresh capital for a new Fokker and invest in the development of a new 125-seat regional jet, but Samsung is said to have baulked at demands for long-term job guarantees in the Netherlands.
Russia's Yakovlev said on Friday it was still optimistic it could buy Fokker, citing a price of around $200-270 million which it could pay with Russian government guarantees.

Fokker, founded in 1919 by Dutch aviation pioneer Anthony Fokker, is one of the oldest names in the industry and its F27 Friendship turboprop, launched in 1957, was one of the industry's biggest commercial successes.
